prerequisites: Knowledge of the basic topics of analysis (limit, derivative, integral, resolution of ordinary differential equations, etc.)
Knowledge of linear algebra (matrixes, Rouche-Capelli theorem, eigenvalues problem, etc.)

learning_outcomes.text: Get sufficient depth knowledge of structural mechanics, covering structures made from any material and any size.
Acquire basic knowledge of mechanics of solids, necessary for mechanical design and for the study of the behavior of machines and mechanisms.
Acquire the foundation for the determination of the stress and strain fields in 3D bodies, of internal forces in structures made by beams, and for the safety checks.
Address standard design problems, applying mathematical methods to model, analyze and solve engineering problems.
Carry out analysis and design of machine parts or simple mechanical systems.
Settle the elastic problem for the determination of stress and strain field in any 3D body.
Correctly interpret the causes of structural behaviors commonly addressed in engineering practice.
Determine the stress field generated inside structures, 3D bodies, and statically determined and undetermined structures, as a result of static loads and distortions.
Assess whether the material is capable of withstanding the stress field generated by external loads.
Apply and further develop acquired skills in mechanical design, applied mechanics, and mechanical technology courses, promoting cross-disciplinary learning.
Solve problems not typical of mechanical engineering, for example, transverse to other branches of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Principle of Virtual Works for rigid bodies
The De Saint-Venant problem and the technical theory of beams
Principle of Virtual Works for deformable bodies
assessment_rules: The learning evaluation consists of a written examination and an oral interview. A minimum score of 18/30 on the written examination is mandatory for admission to the oral examination. The final mark, on a thirty-point scale with possible praise, starts from the written evaluation and is adjusted based on the interview. The minimum passing mark is 18/30 for understanding basic concepts, with the mark increasing with knowledge and elaboration ability up to 30/30 for full knowledge.
